nominees.name: David Crowley

positions.stance: First-30-days plan: repeal Act 10 to restore collective bargaining.
Close the special education funding gap so districts avoid cuts and layoffs.
Universal pre-K and child care using providers already serving families.
Open BadgerCare as a public option for any household, using federal Medicaid match for part of the cost.
Require the largest AI data center operators to pay full grid-upgrade costs.
Won Republican-led Legislature approval to increase state-shared revenue, enabling a 0.4% Milwaukee County sales tax that gave property tax relief.

policyShifts.shift: Repealing Act 10 would reset collective bargaining for state and local employees; it affects school and local-government labor costs and contracts.
BadgerCare public option would be a major expansion of Medicaid-based coverage; needs federal waiver/approval and state authority.
Closing the special-education funding gap changes state aid to school districts and local property tax pressure.
Making data centers pay for grid upgrades shifts cost allocation and affects PSC rate cases and economic-development deals.
Universal pre-K/child care would build on existing providers and requires new state funding and program rules.

impediments.title: Republican legislative majorities
impediments.detail: Before the election Republicans held 18-15 in the Senate and 54-45 in the Assembly; results of the 2026 legislative races were not confirmed here. Act 10 repeal, BadgerCare expansion and new spending need legislative votes.

impediments.title: Funding and federal approval
impediments.detail: The Crowley release gave no dollar amounts or funding sources, and a BadgerCare public option relies on federal Medicaid match and approval.

impediments.title: Executive-vs-legislative split unclear
impediments.detail: The campaign did not say which first-30-days actions are executive orders and which need legislation.

impediments.title: Partisan friction
impediments.detail: His launch video criticized Republican legislative leadership, which may harden opposition even though his county record shows a bipartisan deal.

insights: First-30-days plan makes Act 10 the clearest early signal; whether Democrats flipped any legislative chamber decides how much is reachable (verify post-election results).
Milwaukee County Executive staff are a likely hiring pipeline (inference).

analysis.assumption: Scenario: assumes David Crowley wins the Nov. 3, 2026 general election. AP lookup shows the race called (Nov. 4, 2026 04:34 UTC); this tool does not make calls. Not a call or forecast.
analysis.summary: Crowley would succeed Democrat Tony Evers with a more ambitious labor and health-coverage agenda (Act 10 repeal, BadgerCare public option, special-education funding) than a pure continuity transition. Outcomes depend on legislative control, which was unconfirmed in sources found.
analysis.timing: Inauguration expected early January 2027 (verify); 30-day plan frames early executive and legislative asks.
firstMoves: Name chief of staff and DHS/DPI liaison.
Introduce Act 10 repeal and budget asks.
Begin federal waiver design for BadgerCare.
risks: Republican legislative opposition if chambers held.
